issues.description: The problem statement and template expect concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (used in the UML and the commented Main.java), but the solution repository implements working concrete classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat while the solution's Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java files are empty. This mismatch between expected class names (Seal/Pig/Goat) and the solution's concrete class names (Space*) is structural and may confuse students about which class names to implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the concrete animal class names consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution's SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/Pig/Goat and implement those classes (removing empty placeholders), or (B) update the problem statement and template (including the UML and Main.java comments) to reference SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat. Ensure Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java are not left as empty placeholders in the solution repository.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (the UML and tasks explicitly require classes Seal, Pig, Goat and Main.java in the template instantiates those names), but the solution implementation provides classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead. This creates a mapping confusion: students reading the exercise expect to implement/use Seal/Pig/Goat, while the reference solution uses differently named concrete classes, making it harder to match requirements to the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class names consistent across artifacts. Either (A) rename the solution classes SpaceSeal, SpacePig, SpaceGoat to Seal, Pig, Goat so they match the problem statement and template, or (B) add small wrapper classes named Seal, Pig, Goat in the solution that extend or delegate to the Space* implementations (e.g., public class Seal extends SpaceSeal) so the expected identifiers appear in the solution. Update any references in Main.java or documentation accordingly.
